title: Chapter 1 – Laws of Chess: Mock Exam

questions.text: What is the objective of each player in a game of chess?

options.text: To capture all opponent's pieces
To place the opponent's king under attack with no legal escape
To occupy the centre of the board
To promote a pawn to a queen

questions.explanation: As per Article 1.1, the objective of each player is to place the opponent's king under attack in such a way that the opponent has no legal move. This is called checkmate.

questions.text: How must the chessboard be placed at the start of the game?

options.text: Near corner square to the left of each player must be white
Near corner square to the right of each player must be black
Near corner square to the right of each player must be white
It does not matter which way the board is placed

questions.explanation: As per Article 1.2, the chessboard is placed between the players in such a way that the near corner square to the right of each player is white.

questions.text: What happens if a player arrives after the default time at the start of a session?

options.text: The player receives a warning
The player's clock continues to run
The player shall lose the game unless the arbiter decides otherwise
The game is adjourned

questions.explanation: As per Article 6.7, any player who arrives at the chessboard after the start of the session shall lose the game unless the arbiter decides otherwise. The default time is 0 minutes unless competition rules specify otherwise.

options.text: When a player's king is in check with no legal move
When a player has no legal move and their king is NOT in check
When both players agree to end the game
When only kings remain on the board

questions.explanation: As per Article 9.1, a game is drawn (stalemate) when the player to move has no legal move and their king is NOT in check. This is different from checkmate where the king IS in check.

questions.text: When can a player offer a draw?

options.text: At any time during the opponent's turn
Only before making a move
After making a move on the chessboard, then pressing the clock
Only in the endgame phase

questions.explanation: As per Article 9.2, a draw offer may be made after the player has made a move on the chessboard, then pressing the clock. The offer may not be withdrawn.

questions.text: How many pieces does each player start with?

options.text: 12 pieces
14 pieces
16 pieces
18 pieces

questions.explanation: As per Article 1.3, at the beginning of the game each player has 16 pieces: a king, a queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights, and eight pawns.

questions.text: When can a draw be claimed by threefold repetition?

options.text: When the same position has appeared twice
When the same position is about to appear or has appeared at least three times
When both players have been making the same moves for 10 turns
Only when agreed upon by both players

questions.explanation: As per Article 9.3, a draw can be claimed when the same position is about to appear for the third time (player must write move and declare intention) or has appeared at least three times.
